titre: GTA 6 Sets New Sales Record for Rockstar Just One Day In
chapo: Grand Theft Auto 6 has reportedly made over $2.3 billion in revenue for Rockstar Games so far as it is now finally released.
extrait: Grand Theft Auto 6 was setting records before it was even released. Now that it's out, don't expect that pace to slow down anytime soon. New estimates suggest GTA 6 is not just the fastest-selling video game ever, but the fastest-selling piece of entertainment ever. According to the latest estimates from market analysis firm Sensor Tower, which has been tracking GTA 6 preorders for some time, Rockstar's latest blockbuster game has sold 24.58 million copies. It has generated $2.3 billion, bringing the average GTA 6 sale price to $93.57. That means most players have purchased the more expensive Ultimate Edition ($99.99), although recent purchasers have gravitated toward the standard edition ($79.99). When GTA 6 crossed $1 billion in estimated revenue, the average sale was about $97. Rockstar has not officially announced sales figures for GTA 6 yet. Grand Theft Auto 5 hit $1 billion in revenue in three days, and Rockstar parent company Take-Two said at the time it believed "this marks the fastest that any entertainment property, including video games and feature films, has reached this significant milestone." GTA 6 appears to have surpassed that success. Likewise, Rockstar has not confirmed how big GTA 6's development budget was. The studio has been focused on making the game since releasing Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018. Rockstar previously shot down the idea that GTA 6 cost $1.5 billion to make, but the game likely cost over $1 billion to make, meaning it's the most expensive video game in history. Players have been enjoying discovering all that GTA 6 has to offer, like Easter eggs, bodega cats, and the game's best-kept secret. GTA 6 is out now on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

titre: GTA 6 sales are almost at 25 million as Rockstar earns $2.36 billion in revenue, analysts estimate
chapo: Most of them are on PS5, too

Now that GTA 6 is actually out and people the world over can finally play it, we'll start seeing figures for just how much money Rockstar's new epic is raking in. One set of estimates place current revenue at north of 2.3 billion US dollars, and over 24.5 million copies sold. These numbers come from Sensor Tower, an analytics firm that keeps a live database to track the returns for releases across the industry. Naturally, GTA 6 is getting a healthy amount of attention, and the site is primed with up-to-date amounts. According to the tool, Grand Theft Auto 6 has brought in around $2.36 billion thus far. The bulk of that money will have come from pre-orders, and as of now, the amount of copies sold on all platforms is thought to sit at 24.58 million. I don't think anyone would complain about seeing that kind of consumer response to their game. Sensor Tower provides a platform breakdown too, for where GTA 6 has sold more, and to nobody's surprise PS5 is thought to be in the lead, taking 75% of the copies shifted, whereas the Xbox Series X/S only make up for 25%. That's quite a disparity, but it's one we saw coming well before the game's release date hit. Tracking consistently placed PlayStation 5 sales ahead of the Xbox Series X/S. There are simply more of them out in the world, creating a significantly bigger install base, and Sony went quite hard in terms of partnering with Rockstar and general advertising. I mean, GTA 6 was the startup graphic for the PS5 for a time, and it's been brought back for launch. That's the kind of full-on marketing that pushes people on the fence toward putting their money down. Regardless of how anyone was convinced, there are a lot of players of GTA 6 right now. And just remember, we still have the PC release to go yet, even though Rockstar is yet to confirm it. Rockstar's managed to meet nigh-incomprehensible levels of anticipation with equally ludicrous sales. I look forward to informing you about GTA 6 still being in the charts in a decade's time, just like its predecessor. titre: GTA 6 day-one sales are enormous, estimates suggest, making previous $2 billion opening weekend predictions seem conservative
chapo: Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting . Read more
extrait: Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting. The estimates come from data-tracking company Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects. Should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6. So far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent company Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?". Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."
